title: RADIO LIGHTING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the detailed procedures for securing the dimming control to the circuit panel assembly during installation?
answer: NOTE:  Two dimming control potentiometers are located on the circuit panel assembly. One dimming control serves as the radio lighting  and instrument lighting  dimming control, the second dimming control serves as the glareshield lighting  and pedestal lighting  dimming control. Removal and installation for both dimming controls are typical.Remove Dimming Control . (1) Disconnect the electrical power from the airplane. (2) Make sure the ALT/BAT MASTER switch in the off position. (3) Remove circuit panel assembly.  Refer to Chapter 31, Instrument and Control Panels - Maintenance Practices. (4)  Loosen setscrew on knob and remove knob to access nut securing dimming control to circuit panel assembly. (5) Remove nut securing dimmer control to circuit panel assembly. (6)  Identify, tag and disconnect the wires from the dimming control. (7) Remove dimming control from airplane.Install Dimming Control . (1) Position dimming control and solder labeled wires to proper pins. See Model 182 Wiring Diagram Manual. (2)  Place dimming control through circuit panel assembly and secure with nut. (3)  Position knob on dimming control and set with setscrew. (4) Install circuit panel assembly. Refer to Chapter 31, Instrument and Control Panels - Maintenance Practices. (5) Connect the electrical power to the airplane. (6) Press the ALT/BAT MASTER switch to ON to do a check of the dimming control.Y.: ... :..

title: RADIO LIGHTING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How does the parallel wiring of instrument lights and the PANEL LT dimmer influence their control and illumination?
answer: Panel illumination is operated with independent lights installed in each instrument and gage. The lights are wired parallel and are controlled by the PANEL LT dimmer, found below the navigation indicators. Illumination intensity for the radios is controlled by the TST  - BRT  - DIM  switch. When the switch is in the BRT position, the radio illumination will be off regardless of the RADIO LT dimmer position.

One dimming control serves as the radio lighting  and instrument lighting  dimming control, the second dimming control serves as the glareshield lighting  and pedestal lighting  dimming control. Removal and installation for both dimming controls are typical.Remove Dimming Control . (1) Disconnect the electrical power from the airplane. (2) Make sure the ALT/BAT MASTER switch in the off position. (3) Remove circuit panel assembly.  Refer to Chapter 31, Instrument and Control Panels - Maintenance Practices. (4)  Loosen setscrew on knob and remove knob to access nut securing dimming control to circuit panel assembly. (5) Remove nut securing dimmer control to circuit panel assembly. (6)  Identify, tag and disconnect the wires from the dimming control. (7) Remove dimming control from airplane.Install Dimming Control . (1) Position dimming control and solder labeled wires to proper pins. See Model 182 Wiring Diagram Manual. (2)  Place dimming control through circuit panel assembly and secure with nut. (3)  Position knob on dimming control and set with setscrew. (4) Install circuit panel assembly. Refer to Chapter 31, Instrument and Control Panels - Maintenance Practices. (5) Connect the electrical power to the airplane. (6) Press the ALT/BAT MASTER switch to ON to do a check of the dimming control.Y.: ... :..

title: RADIO LIGHTING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: How does the wiring configuration of instrument and radio lights influence their ability to be controlled separately and what components are involved in this control?
answer: Panel illumination is operated with independent lights installed in each instrument and gage. The lights are wired parallel and are controlled by the PANEL LT dimmer, found below the navigation indicators. Illumination intensity for the radios is controlled by the TST  - BRT  - DIM  switch. When the switch is in the BRT position, the radio illumination will be off regardless of the RADIO LT dimmer position.
